title: OpenHarness: an observable, testable, priced plugin layer for agent behavioral rules
description:
OpenHarness makes one architectural move: it removes behavioral rules from an agent's skills and re-mounts them as a plugin layer above the agent, the way middleware sits above application code. Each rule becomes a harness module with a declared scope (when it binds), a conformance check (was it followed), and a price (what the check costs). Binding is decided by the layer, not by the agent's discretion.

Because a module has boundaries, its activity is loggable (an observable stream of verdicts: event → module bound with evidence → pass/fail) and evaluable as a unit (run a task with the module on and off, count passes and failures per task type, record what each check costs by tier). Accumulated over real usage, every module earns a harness card — competence by task type, live conformance split by severity, enforcement cost and accuracy, a momentum trend, and upstream news — and the cards form a dashboard. The harness stops being an invisible influence and becomes a characterized instrument: a materia medica of harnesses.
